caseAnalysis.title: Release of nine detained HfA surgeons in Beta Town
caseAnalysis.summary: Nine Swiss Health for All (HfA) surgeons are confined to their residence by tribespeople in Beta Town after HfA announced it would end operations there in September and redeploy to Gamma. HfA reports the staff cannot leave until it reaches an agreement with tribal leaders on maintaining health services. The tribal chief has limited talks to the council office and advised against contact with the staff. HfA cites a strict no-ransom policy, depleted funds and donor mandates. It insists on release before discussing the dispute but has said it is willing to seek a compromise. The Swiss Ambassador committed only to ask Bern about special funds for minimal services. Police and the government defer to tribal leaders. No role card identifies which side we represent.

issues.text: No role card was supplied. The package contains prompts for both an HfA-supporting negotiator and the Tribal Leader, so our side is unresolved.
Sequencing conflict: HfA insists on release before discussing the dispute, while HfA also reports that release depends on an agreement on health services.
Swiss special funds for minimal services are not approved. The commitment is only to communicate with Bern.

immediate.text: HfA reports its staff are detained in their residence and unable to leave until HfA and tribal leaders reach an agreement on health service maintenance in the district.

actors.text: HfA delegation: its immediate goal is safe release of the staff; it holds a no-ransom policy and says a long-term presence is not viable.
Tribal chief: demands talks only at the council office and advises against contacting the detained staff until an amicable resolution is reached.
German Ambassador: says compromises on maintaining Beta Town programmes are beyond her authority and should go to Berlin.
Swiss Ambassador: will ask Bern about special funds for minimal hospital services, such as measles support, as a compromise for release.
Police chief: police will not intervene, but will step in to restore peace once a health-services agreement is reached.
Minister of Health: says the matter largely rests with tribal leaders and warns that government interference might escalate tensions.

tension.text: HfA stands firm on redeploying to Gamma, citing depleted funds and donor mandates, while release is tied to an agreement on maintaining local health services.

background.text: HfA publicly announced the transfer of its Country Director and Beta Town personnel to Gamma City.

uncertainty.text: HfA fears possible ransom demands and unpredictable action by local guards if a solution is not found promptly.
The outcome of the Bern request for special funds is unknown.

response_branches.text: If release-first is refused, the documented basis for a parallel discussion of services is HfA's stated willingness to seek a compromise.
If money is demanded, the response is shaped by HfA's no-ransom policy and the Swiss Ambassador's warning against paying ransoms.

critical_assumptions.text: The assumption is that an agreement on health services would lead to release, as both HfA's report and the police chief's statement indicate.

opponent_demands.text: Tribal chief: HfA must reinforce local health authorities' capacity to respond to the measles outbreak.

decision_authority.text: Release decisions rest with the tribal leaders, according to the guard representatives and the Minister.

tradeoffs.proposal: Minimal hospital and measles services funded by Swiss special funds, in exchange for release.
tradeoffs.benefit: Addresses the reported release condition without ransom.
tradeoffs.risk: Bern has not approved the funds, and the Swiss Ambassador doubts the value of scaling down rather than withdrawing.
